vSNP3 GUI · FMDV mode · step-by-step training (SOP)

Type four foot-and-mouth disease virus samples

You will bring in reads and genomes four different ways, let vSNP3 choose a reference for each sample, read its serotype and lineage, and place it on a tree. Every step shows what to do and what you should see.

TIME

About 45 minutes. Half of it is waiting while the two trees build.

YOU NEED

The tools installed (Part A of the vSNP3 GUI training), internet, and about 2 GB of free disk space.

TESTED

19 November 2026, vSNP GUI v0.4.154, vsnp3 3.37, on a Mac. Newer versions may look a little different.

To move: click Next → at the bottom, or press the → arrow key.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

Start

What FMDV mode is

A kind of vSNP3 project made for foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV).

It answers three questions about a sample, in this order:

  1. Which serotype and lineage is it? The sample's reads vote for the closest of 79 lineage genomes.
  2. What is it closest to in GenBank? Its VP1 gene is compared with about 9,000 published VP1 records, and placed on a tree.
  3. How far is it from other samples of the same lineage? The ordinary vSNP3 Step 2: a SNP table and a tree.

Why its own mode?In an ordinary vSNP3 project, one reference genome serves the whole project. That works for M. bovis, where every sample is more than 99% the same as the reference. Two FMDV lineages of one serotype can differ at one base in five, and reads stop mapping long before that. So in FMDV mode the reference is chosen for each sample. Everything after that choice is the vSNP3 you know.

Your other projectsNothing changes for ordinary projects (TB, Brucella and the rest). FMDV mode is a setting of one project.

The samples

Your four samples

All four are public. Two are reads from a sequencer. Two are finished genomes from GenBank.

NumberWhat it isSerotypeComes in by
SRR34371563Nanopore reads. Isolate TAN/27/2012, Tanzania.SAT1the SRA tab
SRR18685705Illumina paired reads. Kenya, 2016.SAT1the SRA tab
EU448369A genome from GenBank. O1/BFS 1860/UK/67, United Kingdom.Othe Sequences tab
HM625673A genome from GenBank. O/K/48/2005, Kenya. It stands in for a consensus genome sent by another laboratory.Othe Sequences tab
You paste them in steps B3 and B4.

Reads or a genome?Reads are what a sequencer makes. A genome is the finished sequence somebody already built from reads. FMDV mode takes both, so you can compare your own samples with a published genome or with a result another laboratory sends you.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

The samples

The plan

Six things, in order.

  1. Set up, once. Build the FMDV reference library (Part A, about 5 minutes).
  2. Create a project in FMDV mode.
  3. Bring in the four samples: two by SRA number, two by GenBank number.
  4. Step 1. Each sample gets its own reference, an alignment, a consensus genome and a serotype and lineage call (about 1 minute).
  5. Step 2, VP1. Build a tree for SAT1 and a tree for O, and read each sample's nearest relatives (about 20 minutes, mostly waiting).
  6. Step 2, whole genome. Compare the two SAT1 samples SNP by SNP.
vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

Part A

Set up FMDV mode

You do this once on each computer. It needs internet.

A laboratory that does not work on FMDV can skip it. Ordinary vSNP3 projects never use it.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

A. Set up (first time only)

A1 · Update the tools

FMDV mode arrived in vSNP GUI v0.4.154.

▶ Do this

Open a terminal in the tools folder and run these two commands, one at a time.

  1. Get the newest tools list:
    bin/bdtools pull
  2. Move vSNP3 to it. This also adds the two extra programs FMDV mode uses (BLAST+ and mafft):
    bin/bdtools update vsnp_gui

Not in the tools folder yet? Run cd ~/bioinformatic_diagnostic_tools first.

✔ You should see

The second command ends by checking the pinned programs. Look for these lines:

Terminal
  ok vsnp_gui: vsnp3 3.37 (pinned)
  ok vsnp_gui: mafft 7.526 (pinned)
  ok vsnp_gui: blast 2.17.0 (pinned)

On the vSNP3 page, the title at the top says vSNP GUI v0.4.154 or a newer number.

From the dashboardThe dashboard's update buttons do the same thing (step B3 of the vSNP3 GUI training). Keep clicking the update it offers until it says everything is up to date.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

A. Set up (first time only)

A2 · Build the FMDV reference library

The library is built on your computer, from public data. It takes about 5 minutes.

▶ Do this

  1. In the same terminal, run:
    bin/bdtools setup-databases fmdv
  2. Wait until the prompt comes back.
  3. On the dashboard, click ↻ Restart on the vSNP3 card, so vSNP3 finds the library.

✔ You should see

Four numbered stages, then:

Terminal
[fmdv library] 1/4 lineage genomes and VP1 panel
[fmdv library] 2/4 primer scheme
[fmdv library] 3/4 GenBank VP1 context sets (a few minutes)
[fmdv library] 4/4 GenBank annotations (NCBI, about two minutes)
[fmdv library] ready: 79 lineage genomes, 79 reference folders
  ok FMDV reference library ready: …/databases/fmdv/fmdv_refs
  ok vsnp_gui: …/refs/fmdv -> …/databases/fmdv/fmdv_refs

What is in it?79 FMDV genomes, about one for each lineage of the seven serotypes, and about 9,000 VP1 sequences from GenBank with their serotype, lineage, country and year. The genomes come from the NanoFMDV project (Shaw et al. 2025); the command downloads them from that project's own page.

It stopped?Run the same command again. It only does the stages that are missing. The last stage needs NCBI; without it everything works except the gene names in Step 2 tables.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

Part B

Run the analysis

B. Run the analysis

B1 · Create a project in FMDV mode

The mode is chosen when the project is made.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Projects › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

On the dashboard, open vSNP3. Scroll down to Projects.

  1. Click the box New project name (e.g. LSDV_India) and type FMDV_training.
  2. In the list beside it, choose FMDV mode (reference chosen per sample). It is the first choice in the list.
  3. Click Create.
  4. Click the new card, FMDV_training_FMDV, to open the project.

✔ You should see

Scroll down to Step 1. Where an ordinary project shows one reference, this one says FMDV mode: choose the lineage reference per sample and 79 genomes in the library.

It says the library was not found?Step 1 shows FMDV reference library not found until Part A is done. Do A2, restart vSNP3 from the dashboard, and reload this page.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B2 · The Inputs panel: four ways in

In an FMDV project the Inputs panel has four tabs. It shows one at a time.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

Scroll to Inputs and click each tab once to see it.

MinKNOW runThe folder a nanopore run wrote. One FASTQ per barcode, named from the sample sheet.
FASTQ filesRead files you already have: link a folder, or drop the files.
SequencesA sequence, not reads: a FASTA or GenBank file, or a GenBank number.
SRAPublic reads, by their SRA number.

✔ You should see

Four tabs on the left. On the right, Ready to run: whatever tab the data comes in by, it lands here.

The small ?Each tab has one sentence of help and a ? beside it. Click the ? for the details.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B3 · Download the two read sets

vSNP3 downloads public reads for you.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

First copy the two SRA numbers:

  1. Click the tab SRA.
  2. Click the box SRR/SRX/SRS accessions (one per line) and paste.
  3. Click Download.

✔ You should see

After about a minute: Download complete, 2 downloaded, and two samples under Ready to run. One is a pair (Illumina), one is a single file (nanopore).

Wrong box?An SRA number starts with SRR, ERR or DRR and means reads. A GenBank number, like EU448369, means a sequence: the SRA tab refuses it and points you to the Sequences tab.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B4 · Import two genomes from GenBank

A sequence comes in by the Sequences tab. One click fetches it and makes its reads.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

First copy the two GenBank numbers:

  1. Click the tab Sequences.
  2. Click the box GenBank accessions, one per line and paste.
  3. Leave Import as on samples. Click Import.
  4. Wait for Imported. It takes a few seconds: vSNP3 fetches both records, finds VP1 in each, and writes the reads.

✔ You should see

Imported. Under Ready to run there are now four samples. The two genomes show paired · R1+R2: vSNP3 made reads from each genome, so that it can go through Step 1 like any sample.

A file insteadA FASTA or GenBank file from another laboratory works the same way: drop it on Choose Files, then Import. To change the name first, click Review first instead: it lists each record with its name in a box, and imports nothing until you click Import 1 record.

Nobody is fooledA sample made from a genome is marked Simulated everywhere from here on, and its quality check reads N/A. Its depth and coverage would only describe the made-up reads.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B5 · If you have a MinKNOW run (optional)

Skip this page if you have no nanopore run folder. The four samples are enough.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. Click the tab MinKNOW run.
  2. Paste the path of the run folder MinKNOW wrote (the one that holds fastq_pass), and click Preview.
  3. Check the table. Change a name if you need to. Untick a barcode you do not want.
  4. Click Import … samples.

The names come from a file sample_sheet.csv in the run folder, with two columns: barcode,sample_id. The tab has a Sample sheet template link.

✔ You should see

One row per barcode: how many files it has, their size, and the name the sample sheet gives it. Nothing is written until you click Import. Then each barcode is one FASTQ under Ready to run.

UnderscoresA name like ETH_SAT1_001 becomes ETH-SAT1-001. vSNP3 cuts a sample name at the first underscore, so the import changes underscores to dashes for you.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B6 · Step 1: grab the samples and run

Step 1 does everything for one sample at a time.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. Under Ready to run, click Grab into Step 1.
  2. Scroll down to Step 1. Leave the three lists on Auto.
  3. Do not tick Nanopore (ONT) reads. vSNP3 sees long reads by itself, sample by sample.
  4. Click Run.

For each sample, Step 1 lets the reads choose the closest of the 79 genomes, aligns to it, calls SNPs, builds a consensus genome, cuts VP1 out of it, and types the VP1 against GenBank.

✔ You should see

The button says Running… with a timer. In the Samples list each sample goes from Not Started to Running to Complete. Four samples take about one minute.

The scope listsAuto means: look at every serotype. If you already know the serotype or the lineage, choosing it narrows the search. You can also pin one genome.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B7 · Read the Step 1 Results

One row for each sample. This is the first answer.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 → Step 1 Results › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. In Step 1 Results, click Refresh.
  2. Click Expand to give the table the whole window. Press Esc to put it back.
ColumnWhat it tells you
QCPASS, REVIEW or FAIL, on lines set for an FMDV genome: how much of the genome is covered, depth, mapping.
Read typeONT (nanopore), Paired (Illumina), or Simulated (made from a genome).
ReferenceThe genome this sample's reads chose. It is different from row to row.
Serotype, LineageWhat the reads voted for.
Topotype (VP1)The typing: the nearest named VP1 record in GenBank.
IdentityHow close the reads are to the chosen reference (1.000 is identical).

✔ You should see

Two SAT1 samples on SAT1-I_KM268899 that PASS, and two serotype O genomes, each on its own reference, marked Simulated with QC N/A.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B8 · Open a sample report

Every sample gets a one-page report. Print it or send it.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 → Step 1 Results › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. In the row of SRR34371563, click Files.
  2. Beside FMDV report, click HTML. It opens in a new tab. (PDF is the same page, ready to print.)

The same list of files has the Stats workbook and IGV, which shows the reads on the reference so that you can check any SNP with your own eyes.

✔ You should see

The call at the top, then the quality numbers, the reference, the nearest relatives, and VP1. After you build the trees (B9), the report also carries a small tree.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B9 · Step 2: build the VP1 trees

In an FMDV project, Step 2 starts with VP1, because serotype and lineage are defined on VP1.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

Scroll down to Step 2. The tab VP1 is open. The table VP1 typing says 4 of 4 typed.

  1. Under VP1 tree, choose SAT1 (2 samples) in the list.
  2. Click Build VP1 tree. Wait about 4 minutes.
  3. Then choose O (2 samples) and click Build VP1 tree again. The O tree is bigger: about 15 minutes on a laptop.

✔ You should see

While a tree builds, Live Logs at the bottom of the page shows its progress (Bootstrap[1] … Bootstrap[99], then a quiet few minutes).

When it is done, Step 2 Results shows a button for each tree, with its date.

One tree for each serotypeA tree holds your samples of one serotype, the library's genomes, and GenBank records chosen to cover every lineage of that serotype, plus each sample's nearest relatives.

You can keep workingThe tree builds in the background. While you wait for the O tree, go on to B10 with the SAT1 tree.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B10 · Open the tree

The tree shows where your samples sit among everything known.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 → Step 2 Results › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. In Step 2 Results, click the button of the SAT1 tree, then the view Tree.
  2. Click Neighbourhood tree. It opens in a new tab.
  3. Find the two highlighted names: your samples.

The neighbourhood tree keeps your samples, their nearest records, and one record for each other lineage, so that you can read every name. The full tree, with every record, is the button beside it.

✔ You should see

SRR34371563 sits right beside MT602086.1 and the Tanzania 2012 records. SRR18685705 sits among the Kenya 2016 records. Both are in topotype I.

Reading itA short line between two names means few differences. Numbers on the branches are bootstrap support: 70 or more is a group you can trust.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B11 · Neighbours and sites

The same answer as the tree, as tables.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 → Step 2 Results › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. Back on the vSNP3 page, in Step 2 Results, click the O tree (when it is done), then Neighbours.
  2. Then click Sites.

Neighbours lists, for each sample, the records within 3% of its nearest one, with country, year and host.

Sites shows the VP1 positions that differ among your samples and their neighbours, as amino acids or nucleotides. Open it as a table with Open.

✔ You should see

For EU448369: nearest O-EURO-SA-O1_AY593815 at 100%, and a list of United Kingdom records from 1967 and 1968. That is right: EU448369 is the 1967 UK outbreak virus.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B12 · Whole-genome SNPs for one lineage

The second tab is the ordinary vSNP3 Step 2. It compares samples that share a reference.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. In Step 2, click the tab Genome SNPs: build.
  2. In box 0, Compare on reference, choose SAT1-I_KM268899 (2 samples).
  3. Click Build comparison set, then scroll down and click Run.

✔ You should see

The panel says the two O samples are left out: they are on other references. After under a minute, Step 2 Results → Genome SNPs lists the groups, each with a tree and SNP tables, as in any vSNP3 project.

Reference databasesTwo samples alone say little. A laboratory that works on FMDV builds, once for each reference it uses, the other genomes of that serotype as reference databases (the tick boxes in box 2; docs/FMDV_MODE.md in the vsnp_gui repository, “Step 2 context”, has the three commands). In the pictures here they are ticked: 8 lineage genomes and 39 GenBank genomes of SAT1. Without them your table has 2 samples and the steps are the same.

What it showsWith the databases, SRR34371563 is 0 SNPs from MT602086.1, the published genome of the same isolate, and 6 from the reference. The next genome is more than 380 SNPs away. Same virus, to within sequencing error: that is what a whole-genome comparison can say and a VP1 tree cannot.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

B. Run the analysis

B13 · The run report

One page for the people who must act on the result.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 → Step 1 Results › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. At the top of Step 1 Results, beside FMDV run report, click HTML.

It is rewritten each time Step 1 or a tree finishes, so it is always the current state of the project. PDF is the same page for printing.

✔ You should see

A summary in words (which serotypes and lineages are present, which samples share one), one table of calls with notes, then a tree for each serotype with your samples highlighted.

C. Finish

C1 · Check yourself

Click a question to see the answer.

1. Why does each sample get its own reference in FMDV mode?

FMDV lineages are too different from one another. Reads from one lineage do not map well to the genome of another, so one reference for the whole project would lose most samples.

2. Which reference did the two SAT1 samples choose?

SAT1-I_KM268899, the library's genome for SAT1 topotype I.

3. EU448369 shows QC “N/A”. Is something wrong?

No. It came in as a genome, and its reads were made from that genome. Depth and coverage would describe the made-up reads, so no quality verdict is given. It is marked Simulated.

4. What is SRR34371563 closest to on VP1?

MT602086.1, at 100%. That is the published genome of the same isolate, TAN/27/2012.

5. Serotype, lineage, SNP distance: which one can say two samples are the same virus?

Only the SNP distance over the whole genome (B12). Serotype and lineage place a sample among everything known; they do not separate two close viruses.

vSNP3 GUI training, FMDV mode · Kapur Lab · Penn State

C. Finish

C2 · If something goes wrong

Most problems have a simple fix.

ProblemFix
The reference list has no FMDV mode choicevSNP3 is older than v0.4.154. Do A1.
Step 1 says FMDV reference library not foundDo A2, then restart vSNP3 from the dashboard and reload the page.
setup-databases fmdv says the environment lacks blastnRun bin/bdtools install vsnp_gui, then the same command again. On a shared install, ask the administrator: the test data page has the two commands.
After Step 1, the VP1 tab of Step 2 lists only the two imported genomes (2 of 2 typed)vSNP3 is older than v0.4.162. Reload the page, or do A1: from v0.4.162 the tab follows Step 1 by itself.
A red Reference check lists several references and Run is disabled, telling you to choose a reference in the Projects panelNothing is wrong. Do B12: on Genome SNPs: build, choose the lineage in box 0, Compare on reference. From v0.4.164 the page says this itself.
Step 2 Results shows no Typing, Tree, Neighbours, Sites or FilesNo VP1 tree has been built yet: those views belong to a tree. Do B9.
The Sequences tab says the FMDV reference library has not been built on this install, or no VP1 panel at …/fmdv_refs/panels/vp1.fastaA2 was not done on this computer, or it was done and vSNP3 cannot see the result. Do A2 (again, if need be: a second run takes seconds). Its last lines say whether vSNP3 finds the library. Then click Import again.
The Sequences tab says Nothing was imported: BLAST+ (blastn) is missingThe same cause: BLAST+ is missing. Fix it as in the row above, then click Import again.
The Sequences tab has a Preview button and no Import buttonvSNP3 is older than v0.4.159. Do A1. Until then: click Preview, then Import 2 records.
Downloading… for many minutes and nothing new under Ready to runvSNP3 is older than v0.4.156. Do A1, then paste the SRA numbers again and click Download. From v0.4.156 a stalled download carries on by itself, and Stop ends it.
Review first on the Sequences tab shows no Serotype or VP1 columnsThe open project is not an FMDV project. Open FMDV_training_FMDV.
The Sequences tab says NCBI is unreachableThe computer is offline. Records already fetched once still work. Otherwise drop the FASTA or GenBank file.
A record is refused as too short or no VP1It is a fragment. A sample needs a genome, or at least a whole VP1.
Build VP1 tree is paleAnother job is running, or no sample of that serotype has VP1. Wait, or check the VP1 typing table.
A sample in Step 1 says ErrorClick View log beside it. To try again, tick Force re-run and click Run.
Anything elseIn the tools folder, run bin/bdtools doctor vsnp_gui: it lists what is wrong and the command that fixes it.
